```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B names a concrete payer: IT staff, clerks and ADA coordinators at municipalities facing dated federal deadlines of April 2027 and April 2028, each cited to ADA.gov and the Federal Register. A says outright it has no defined payer and no evidence of an institutional buyer.",
    "B shows money already changing hands. Cole County, MO paid $7,000 for a compliance tool in March 2026. The Town of Templeton was quoted $2,510 for an AudioEye add-on. GovAccess publishes $149/month. A's only price anchor is Yoodli's $8–20/month consumer tiers, and several direct competitors in A (Noora, SpringSocial, Talkville) are free or freemium.",
    "B's demand evidence comes from named officials quoted in a local newspaper about a real mandate. A's demand evidence is two anonymous Reddit comments and a testimonial taken from a competitor's own marketing page.",
    "A's unit economics look weak on its own numbers. It cites $20–50 per user through ASO and agency fees of $10k–18k/month, against an $8/month price with no retention data. B's per-deal value of roughly $900–$7,000 can carry a few hand-sold, high-touch deals inside 90 days.",
    "Both ideas face entrenched competitors and commodity tech. B's incumbents, however, confirm buyers will pay. A's free, Stanford-backed incumbent caps what anyone will pay.",
    "B has real risks: slow municipal procurement, E&O liability for compliance claims, and possible further deadline slippage. Its own brief lists these and gives no source for the procurement-speed claim. They threaten the 90-day timeline but do not undercut the evidence of demand. A's core problem, an undefined customer, is more basic."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's strongest-looking demand signal is the App Store review ('After 3 weeks of daily warmups, I just... do it now'). It was surfaced on Convo's own marketing page, so it is self-selected promotional copy for a competitor. It says nothing about willingness to pay for a new entrant or about any specific segment. A's acquisition figures are also internally inconsistent: ASO at $20–50/user is called the cheapest channel besides referral, yet Apple Search Ads is cited at ~$3.76 CPA.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B clearly has stronger evidence of payment and a defined payer. Its fit with a 90-day first sale is uncertain, though. The brief flags slow municipal procurement, insurance requirements and liability exposure, and gives no evidence that a solo vendor can close within 90 days or buy under small-purchase thresholds. If procurement proves as slow as feared, B could miss the window. A would likely still fail, because it has no defined customer."
}
```
